full_judgment:
14. Mr Chowdhury, upon placing the first information report and charge sheet, submits that some of the important first information report named as well as charge sheet named witnesses namely Md Faruque, Salma Begum, Monwara Begum, Md Russell and Md Asgar Ali were not examined in this case without any reasonable explanation, which raises a presumption against the prosecution to the effect that had they been examined they would not support the prosecution case. Mr Hoque further submits that the learned tribunal Judge most illegally, relying on the so-called statement of the condemned prisoner Kala Palash as recorded in Audio Cassette (Exhibit IV) by the investigating officer, found the convict appellant and others were guilty which cannot be sustained in law whatsoever, inasmuch as the statement of audio cassette does not carry any legal value in the eye of law. Moreover, the statement of Kala Palash as recorded in Audio Cassette is product of inhuman torture, threat and coercion under the police custody. The learned Advocate further submits that in this case the blood-stained earth, wearing clothes of the deceased Mizan were not seized to show that an occurrence took place in a particular place with such weapon and in such a manner as narrated by the prosecution thus, it can be safely said the occurrence did not take place as alleged by the prosecution. 

 25. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, after referring the provisions of section 16 of the Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002, submits that the learned trial Judge committed no illegality in considering the audio cassette (Exhibit IV) as evidence, inasmuch as section 16 of the Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 itself speaks that video cassette or audio cassette or still picture with regard to the occurrence is admissible in evidence. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that mere non-examination of some of the first information report named witnesses does not raise a presumption against the prosecution case, while a number of eye-witnesses as well as victim of the occurrence in their respective testimony consistently stated the manner of the occurrence. Finally, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits with force that in view of the evidence of the victims namely, PW 3 and PW 4, coupled with statements of star accused Kala Polash as recorded in audio cassette (Exhibit IV) and evidence of PWs the prosecution has proved the case of committing murder by the condemned prisoners, which they did intentionally and such intention is apparent from the nature of injuries proved by PWs 12 and 18 and hence the appellants have rightly been convicted under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code by the Druta Bichar Tribunal and therefore, the Death Reference should be accepted.
